definition.def: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.
examples: He didn't integrate successfully into the Italian way of life. [V + into/with]
Integrating the kids with the community, finding them a role, is essential. [V n + into/with]
The way Swedes integrate immigrants is, she feels, 100% more advanced. [VERB noun]
If they want to integrate, that's fine with me. [VERB]

definition.def: When races integrate or when schools and organizations are integrated, people who are Black or belong to ethnic minorities can join White people in their schools and organizations. [US]
examples: Schools came to us because they wanted to integrate. [VERB]
Encouraging teacher transfer would not, by itself, integrate the teaching corps. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you integrate one thing with another, or one thing integrates with another, the two things become closely linked or form part of a whole idea or system. You can also say that two things integrate.
examples: ...the problem of integrating the spoken passages with the musical numbers. [VERB noun + with]
Ann wanted the conservatory to integrate with the kitchen. [VERB + with]
Little attempt was made to integrate the parts into a coherent whole. [VERB noun + into]
Talks will now begin about integrating the activities of both companies. [VERB noun]

definition.def: the act or process of combining two or more things so that they work together
examples: The aim is to promote closer economic integration.
His music is an integration of tradition and new technology.

definition.def: the act or process of mixing people who have previously been separated, usually because of colour, race, religion, etc.
examples: measures to promote the social integration of people with learning difficulties
the integration of disabled students into the general education system
